messages:
Ivy: Quick note: support has a case where console shows a feature-flag as "on" for a service but runtime reports it as off. Small repro attached.
Tom: Hmm. Is this the new phased rollout logic interacting with scope inheritance?
Ivy: Looks like it. Console applies a local override and the UI immediately reflects it, but the server-side rollout predicate evaluated at apply-time excludes the org because of an embargo rule. Console isn't surfacing that predicate result.
Rach: We should do two things: (1) add an evaluate endpoint that returns the final resolved value plus provenance and reason for rejection; (2) surface that result inline in the console with a short reason like "rejected by rollout predicate: embargoed_org".
Tom: Agree. Also add telemetry events: `config.evaluate.request`, `config.evaluate.result`, and `config.apply.rejection` with tags for predicate_id, org_id, field.
Ivy: For UX, show a badge that reads "will not apply" with a link "why" which opens the predicate explanation. Avoid modal friction.
Rach: Implementation notes: evaluate must be idempotent and side-effect free for on-prem. Cache evaluations by (scope, candidate_sha) with 30s TTL. Rate-limit per-org.
Tom: Rollout plan: enable evaluate for internal orgs, monitor `console_discrepancy_rate`, then enable for 10% customers. If discrepancy spikes, auto-disable console previews.
infra-bot: deploy: evaluate-service canary deployed at 2024-04-12T11:03:00Z  id ev-2024-04-12-canary
Ivy: I'll add a small support doc explaining "why console shows value but runtime doesn't". Rach, can you own telemetry panels?
Rach: Yup. I'll add a graph for `config.apply.rejection` and an alert when any org > 20 rejections/hour.
Tom: Quick security note: strip any secret references from evaluate responses.
Ivy: Thanks team. This should cut down a bunch of support noise. :raised_hands:
